requirements.requirement: Existing data under /srv/inventory owned by inventorysvc
requirements.summary: Baseline showed root:root ownership (cmd-e49614d79cee4800). Executor created system user inventorysvc (cmd-7042375f34aa4794), applied chown -R inventorysvc:inventory-readers (cmd-27072495cad1400d), and verified via ls -ld showing inventorysvc as owner on the directory, subdirectory, and both files (cmd-e0ab9fad5a4b4b18), confirmed again post-restart (cmd-e2af70918c314175).

Group inventory-readers was created (cmd-6eeadb7f83704f86) and set as the group owner of the tree via chown -R, with directories set to 750 (rwxr-x---) and files to 640 (rw-r-----), giving group read/traverse access. Verified via ls -ld output on cmd-e0ab9fad5a4b4b18 and reconfirmed post-restart on cmd-e2af70918c314175.

chmod 750 on directories and 640 on files (cmd-27072495cad1400d) leaves no permission bits for 'other'. ls -ld output in cmd-e0ab9fad5a4b4b18 confirms drwxr-x--- and -rw-r----- for all tree entries, with no world-readable/executable bits, reconfirmed after restart in cmd-e2af70918c314175.

Baseline file sizes were 40 bytes (records.csv) and 32 bytes (config.json) per cmd-e49614d79cee4800. Post-repair cat output in cmd-e0ab9fad5a4b4b18 shows identical byte sizes and content (sku-1001/1002 rows and {site:north, generation:4}), reconfirmed identically after restart in cmd-e2af70918c314175. Exact sha256 hashes from the prepare baseline were not re-computed by the executor, so byte-for-byte confirmation relies on matching file sizes and visible content rather than a hash comparison.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task — ownership by inventorysvc, group-readability for inventory-readers, no access for other users, and preservation of existing data — are directly demonstrated by before/after command evidence and reconfirmed after a full restart cycle. The independently-required node-restart evidence protocol was executed correctly and completely, with a clear pre-restart baseline, acknowledged reboot, observed disconnection, a changed boot identity, and confirmed recovery of ownership, permissions, and data, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is high, with only a trivial leftover /tmp/reboot.log file as a minor residue.
limitations: Content preservation is confirmed via matching file sizes and visible content across before/after/post-restart checks, not via a direct sha256 comparison against the prepare-stage baseline hashes.
A small /tmp/reboot.log artifact from the backgrounded reboot command was left behind and not cleaned up, though it is low-risk and unrelated to /srv/inventory.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command trace shows a clean, minimal remediation: discovery (cmd-e49614d79cee4800, cmd-ae1aafbc95ea4137), group/user creation (cmd-6eeadb7f83704f86, cmd-7042375f34aa4794), chown/chmod (cmd-27072495cad1400d), and verification (cmd-e0ab9fad5a4b4b18). The first useradd attempt in cmd-6eeadb7f83704f86 failed (referenced a nonexistent 'inventorysvc' group before the user existed) but made no state change beyond the intended groupadd, and was immediately corrected in cmd-7042375f34aa4794 — not an unnecessary mutation. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol (cmd-7914819a040c434e baseline, cmd-7ec1c5ff247148f0 reboot trigger, cmd-3196f4434a6245c0/cmd-fe37a326d68e4ace disconnection, cmd-31241332f4e34eaf new boot id, cmd-e2af70918c314175 recovery) is complete and well-formed, cross-checked by the global boot-identity snapshots (before_prepare/after_prepare e31962a9... vs after_executor 9851f050...). The only residue is a small /tmp/reboot.log left from the backgrounded reboot command (visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot) — a low-risk, non-security-relevant artifact that was not cleaned up. No failed services, no package-manager damage, and no security-control weakening were observed in the after_executor snapshot relative to after_prepare (dnf healthy, no failed units, socket/tmp changes are expected reboot side effects).
